hypothesis: Mimus runs through the SunstoneOS application kit from its own repository and passes recorded and paced acceptance on port 3-1 with seven secondary CPUs off.
narrative: The acceptance branch port/sunstoneos-acceptance-on-split is based on CPU engine revision 0cbc96950; the recorded result uses SunstoneOS e124d65f and the paced image uses 8008acb1. One recorded 57,440-sample input on port 3-1 (entry 1793516356151336408-cac6790a) returns normally with seven secondary CPUs off and complete reference parity: 90 frames, transcript "There was silence.", compute 135.673 ms against the 179.5 ms limit. A paced replay of the same input passes six fresh native sessions (control 1793560017211439012-ff8c6091 and repeats 1793560102532814944-02caa432, 1793560276720214904-91d5e0c3, 1793560482537824782-7589f457, 1793560555177262469-0e251bd4, 1793560636888545789-06c0bafb) with full segmented parity, complete version 2 thermal reports and rail cleanup; median compute is 92.670 ms. These runs do not qualify corpus latency, retained-state replay, sustained multi-utterance capture or thermal and fault recovery. The metadata watcher path issue is worked around with the direct-result workaround in cadence-1101/metadata-watch-note.md.

The input is the first 327,360 samples of LibriSpeech dev-clean 174-84280-0004 (a real utterance, trimmed by 70 ms of its end; 2,047 feature frames, 512 encoder frames), with the all-int8 models int8_a16_punct that the encoder test's graphs come from; the manifest declares the recording region as 654,764 bytes with its digest from inputs-512.json, 0x45000000 to 0x450a002c, before the next region at 0x45100000. What the application does: the OS authenticates the three input regions (14.7 MB), the main task and seven workers wait for the CPU clock grant, pack the weights, recognize the speech (front end, subsampling, 16 conformer layers, CTC head, punctuation) with ss_progress at every checkpoint, park the workers and ss_finish returns the transcript; the OS retires the secondaries and returns to the boot ROM. What it records: the transcript lines (RESULT with CRCs, frames, samples and compute time; TEXT, FORMATTED, PROFILE per stage, MEMORY, CLOCK, BALANCE) decoded by apps/mimus-board/result.py against the reference of this input, which is the host run and the eight-core QEMU run (they agree). Times, from the board record 1793649945122373854-e37cab9b (the same CPU path at the same clocks on 504 frames of joined utterances: 585.067 ms), with the linear stages scaled by 512/504 and the attention core by its square: frontend 9.0 ms, subsample 161.5, feed-forward 97.4, attention 235.3 (core 162.9), convolution module 77.0 (depthwise 60.5), head 9.7, punctuation 1.1, layer norm 3.4, residual 14.0, the 16 layers together (compute minus front end, subsampling, head and punctuation) 415.6, and compute_us 597 ms, within 8 percent (550 to 645 ms); load_us about 92 ms; arena_peak about 4.05 MB, heap peak about 104 KB, yields about 390. The scaling from the 90-frame record (1794092704290307190-d4d3543d) with the recorded split predicts 912 ms (layers 728, attention 471, feed-forward 138, convolution module 111, subsample 165), which I do not use: the 90-frame attention core ran at a fifth of the multiply-accumulate rate of the feed-forward stage (68.4 M multiply-accumulates in 13.4 ms against 713.7 M in 24.2 ms), and the 504-frame record shows the rate rising with the matrices, so the square law overstates it by 1.6 times; the multiply-accumulate counts of the eight-core QEMU run at 512 frames do scale as the recorded split says (feed-forward 5.689 times the 90-frame count, attention core 32.36 times). A compute_us outside 550 to 645 ms, or any stage more than 15 percent from its prediction, misses the prediction. Time budget against the deadlines the code sets: 60 s session (run_us 0, return reserve 5 s, startup 1 s, setup 2 s), finish_by 55 s, supervisor return cutoff 55 s, progress window 3 s. After main starts: input authentication under 0.1 s, clock wait under 0.5 s and at most 1 s, weight packing 0.09 s, recognition 0.60 s, worker stop and finish under 0.1 s, so about 0.9 s and under 3 s even at twice the predicted compute time, against the 55 s finish_by. Longest gap between ss_progress calls: the engine checkpoints between its parallel ranges (387 yields over the 504-frame run, one every 1.5 ms on average); even if the compute phase made no checkpoint at all the gap would be the compute time, 0.6 s predicted and under 1.3 s at twice that, so the gap stays within about 0.4 of the 3 s window at the worst and about 0.01 of it on average. The deadlines nest: 1 s clock wait inside the 3 s progress window inside the 55 s finish_by inside the 60 s session. Uploads dominate: the image is 11.1 MB and the inputs 14.7 MB (the 90-frame run, 14.2 MB, took 75.7 s), so the run total is about 77 s; a run past 95 s fails the prediction.
